mechanism_narrative: Broad re-opening momentum: TRANSIT improving 7.6 points and WORKPLACES improving 9.7 points in the latest week show commuting routines restarting, which mechanically raises weekday retail-and-recreation footfall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -52.0 at t-1w to -44.4 at t-0w
fact:WORKPLACES rose from -42.3 at t-1w to -32.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is at or below its last-28-day mean despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improving in the latest week.

mechanism_narrative: The fall in RESIDENTIAL from 16.7 to 11.6 breaks the stay-at-home plateau; once RESIDENTIAL prints below 12, households shift consumption out of the home and into stores, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 12 (16.7 at t-2w to 11.6 at t-0w)
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 5.1 points from t-2w (16.7) to t-0w (11.6)
failure_condition: In the weeks after RESIDENTIAL first prints below 12, the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean is lower than the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES now move together upward (+7.6 and +9.7 points in the latest week) after diverging earlier; this joint commuting recovery is the gate for discretionary retail traffic, so RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks only when both series improve in the same week.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved week-on-week at t-0w after moving in opposite directions at t-1w
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve, the following 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM recovering from -24.6 to -10.0 is the fastest-normalising errand series; a weekly mean above -15 in GROCERY_PHARM leads RETAIL_REC by one week as routine shopping trips resume.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean rises above -15 (-15.3 at t-1w to -10.0 at t-0w)
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 5.3 points week-on-week to -10.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM is above -15, the one-week-ahead RETAIL_REC mean is equal to or below the trailing four-week RETAIL_REC mean.

mechanism_narrative: The mid-January seasonal trough in indoor discretionary activity ends after the holiday period; PARKS rising 13.9 points to -10.0 shows outdoor movement normalising first, and retail traffic follows with a seasonal rebound over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -23.9 at t-1w to -10.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: In a post-holiday January window where PARKS rises more than 10 points week-on-week, the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean does not exceed the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: If containment policy re-tightens, it first shows up as TRANSIT falling back below -50 for two consecutive weeks; that re-tightening removes discretionary trips and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean falls back below -50 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was below -50 at t-3w (-54.6), t-2w (-58.9) and t-1w (-52.0) before recovering to -44.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: After TRANSIT closes below -50 for two consecutive weeks, the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is equal to or higher than the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL still printing +11.6 while WORKPLACES recovers to -32.6 shows hybrid work is sticky; because home-anchored days redistribute spending toward nearby retail, RETAIL_REC rises as long as RESIDENTIAL stays above +10 and WORKPLACES keeps improving simultaneously.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES recovered from -63.9 at t-2w to -32.6 at t-0w while RESIDENTIAL remained above 11
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is lower than its last-28-day mean in weeks where RESIDENTIAL is above +10 and WORKPLACES improves week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-Omicron wave-decay regime the rebound is led by low-density categories; PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both improving by more than 5 points in the same week predicts a higher RETAIL_REC mean over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM each rise more than 5 points week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 13.9 points and GROCERY_PHARM rose 5.3 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: When PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both rise more than 5 points in the same week during wave decay, the following 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the prior 28-day mean.
